message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Optional hardening: validate attachment_id against ^(att)?\d+$ before building the URL.
reason: The host is the operator-configured Confluence base URL; attachment_id only changes the path on that same host, so a tool argument cannot point the request at internal services or cloud metadata.

message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Optional hardening: reject absolute download URLs whose host differs from config.url.
reason: download_url is taken from the configured Confluence server's own API response (_links.download), not from a tool argument; relative links are joined to the configured base URL.

message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Optional hardening: reject absolute download URLs whose host differs from config.url.
reason: The URL comes from attachment metadata returned by the configured Confluence server, not from the tool argument (content_id only selects which page's attachments to list).

title: Unauthenticated HTTP clients choose the Atlassian base URL via X-Atlassian-Jira-Url / X-Atlassian-Confluence-Url headers
reason: Any client of the HTTP transport (no other auth needed, any token value) can send X-Atlassian-Jira-Url: http://169.254.169.254/ or an internal host; the server builds a fetcher for that URL and immediately makes requests to it, giving SSRF to cloud metadata and internal services, with errors echoed back.
fix: Only accept header-supplied URLs that match an operator allowlist (e.g. ALLOWED_ATLASSIAN_HOSTS, *.atlassian.net), require https, resolve the host and block private/loopback/link-local ranges, and disable redirects for this validation call.

title: Upload tools read any server-side file and send it to Jira/Confluence (local file exfiltration)
reason: file_path / attachments are tool arguments only turned into absolute paths and checked for existence; a prompt injection in an issue or page can make the agent upload ~/.ssh/id_rsa, the server's .env (Atlassian tokens) or /proc/self/environ as an attachment to a page or issue the attacker can read. In HTTP mode this also lets any remote client read the server host's files.
fix: Restrict uploads to a configured upload directory: Path(file_path).resolve() then require is_relative_to(UPLOAD_ROOT.resolve()); refuse symlinks; or disable path-based uploads in HTTP mode and accept base64 content instead.

title: HTTP transports bind to 0.0.0.0 by default
reason: With sse/streamable-http the server listens on all interfaces by default, so anyone on the network can reach the tools (and M001/M002) and, when global credentials are configured, act with the operator's Atlassian account.
fix: Default --host to 127.0.0.1 and require an explicit flag plus an authentication layer to listen publicly.

title: Issue, comment and page bodies are returned to the model unmarked
reason: Jira/Confluence content written by other users is returned straight into the model context while the same server exposes write and upload tools (M002) with no confirmation; whether this matters depends on who can write to the connected spaces/projects.
fix: Run with READ_ONLY_MODE=true or ENABLED_TOOLS for agents that read untrusted content, and require human approval for upload/update/delete tools in the client.
